transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place. No matter
your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your
way with Schwab. This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour. Live from
NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. Facing bipartisan backlash, President Trump's
calling off plans to livestream former army officer Nidal Hassan's execution
for the 2009 Fort Hood shootings and Piers Frank Ordonez reports. President
Trump approved of the execution of Hassan by firing squad. He said he thought
the streaming of the execution might have been a strong deterrent, but he
announced this morning that many good and well-meaning people would rather not
watch him die. He wrote, "He will die as scheduled by firing a squad, but this
event will not be streamed." The announcement is likely to bring some
relief to critics who raised concerns about stoking anti-American propaganda
and that the U.S. was following in the footsteps of regimes in Iran and
Afghanistan that carried out public executions. Eight out of ten Americans
opposed the idea of livestreaming the execution. According to an ABC News
Washington Post poll, Franco Ordonez, NPR News. Ukrainian President Vladimir
Zelensky says he's no longer going along with President Trump's demand for an
energy infrastructure truce. Ukraine's resumed attacks on Russia's oil
refineries. In an interview with the Financial Times, Zelensky says he lost
patience after Ukraine was denied the usual Western intelligence on Russian
ballistic missile strikes and restrictions were placed on Ukraine's
use of U.S.-made Starlink communications. Prices are rising, but people in the U.S.
are still spending. The Commerce Department Census Bureau is posting an
increase in retail sales in September. Here's NPR's Katie Aritle. Retail spending
rose by eight-tenths of a percent last month. Much of this was at the pump. Gas
station spending alone jumped by 6.4 percent. Spending at grocery stores and
restaurants also rose slightly. These numbers don't necessarily mean Americans
are buying more. Inflation is driving up the cost of most goods. The data does
indicate, however, that consumers are resilient. Some analysts stress that while
the economy is on solid footing overall, the burden of inflation is not
distributed equally. Lower and middle-income families are feeling a
significant strain. Katie Aritle, NPR News. Human rights groups are urging
social media platforms not to comply with Turkish court orders to block
hundreds of accounts that belong to journalists and activists. Here's NPR's
Hadil al-Shalchi. Rights groups, including Human Rights Watch, said the
orders against independent media and activists were aimed to restrict freedom
of speech. The appeal comes after a Wednesday raid by Turkish authorities on
a broadcaster that is not aligned with a government called Halk TV. The Committee
to Protect Journalists said that the broadcaster's owner was under
investigation for allegations of bribery, which he denies. Rights groups say
Turkish authorities have increased their crackdown on independent social media
accounts, journalists, and academics, particularly LGBTQ+ groups.
Hadil al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul. From Washington, this is NPR News. In
Britain, booksellers are debating a publisher's decision to no longer
distribute Sally Rooney's books. The Irish novelist says her books can no
longer be sold in the UK because she financially supports the band group
Palestine Action. Rooney has authored four novels, including Conversations with
Friends and Normal People, both of which the BBC adapted for television. Her
books have sold millions of copies. The Milwaukee Brewers are now one win away
from advancing to Major League Baseball's World Series. Last night in Los
Angeles, the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 to take a three-game sit-down lead in
the National League Championship Series. C. Futterman reports the Dodgers have won
the last two World Series titles. The Dodgers dream of creating a modern
baseball dynasty and becoming the first team to win three straight World Series
since 2000 is still alive, but just barely. For the third straight game, the
Brewers use timely hitting to beat LA. Only one Major League team has ever come
back to win a seven-game series after losing the first three, the 2004 Boston
Red Sox. Dodger manager Dave Roberts was on that team. Well, it's certainly
possible. I've lived it. We just got to get a win and we got to find a way to
build some momentum. The Dodgers have baseball's largest payroll and some
believe the team's dominance in large part due to its lavish spending has been
bad for the game. For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles. The winner of
the NLCS will play the winner of the American League Championship Series in
this year's Fall Classic. I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News in Washington. This message
comes from IXL. IXL provides personalized learning and powerful insights that help
teachers boost achievement and understand student progress in real time.
Learn more at IXL.com/NPR.

topics.text: President Trump cancels livestreaming of Nidal Hasan's firing squad execution after bipartisan backlash
Zelensky ends compliance with Trump's energy infrastructure truce, resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries
US retail sales rise 0.8% in September, driven largely by gas station spending
Human rights groups urge social media platforms to resist Turkish orders blocking journalists' and activists' accounts
Sally Rooney's books pulled from UK distribution over her support for Palestine Action
Milwaukee Brewers beat Dodgers 6-2, take 3-0 lead in NLCS
